summary: Gave myseliasan's per-node access grant (NodeAccessGrant) a third rung, CanOperate, so the control plane can map a fleet user onto a node's operator role instead of being forced into the node's admin or viewer role -- completing the fleet half of Tier 2 phase R (the mymatasan-side role model shipped in a prior change). The three flags are now an explicit escalation ladder (CanWrite implies CanOperate implies CanRead), enforced on save by services/node_access.go's normalizeAccess so a grant can never express an incoherent state like write-without-read, and re-normalised on read so a stale or hand-edited row cannot either. NodeAccess.Role() resolves the ladder to the role NAME sent over the tunnel (viewer/operator/admin), which the node evaluates against its own permission matrix -- the control plane never asserts a permission set, only an identity claim. The node_access_api.go audit trail now records the resolved (post-normalization) grant rather than the raw request body, since the two can differ. myseliasan's central RBAC Node Access matrix (RolesAccessPage) and its per-node access dropdown now expose all three levels.
compatibility: Existing NodeAccessGrant rows get canOperate=false by construction (SQLite/Postgres/MariaDB all default a new bool column to false), so no existing grant silently gains the operator capability on upgrade -- a role that previously resolved to viewer or admin continues to resolve exactly the same way; only a superadmin explicitly picking the new Operator level in the Node Access matrix, or POSTing canOperate=true, grants it. The POST /api/nodes/access request body gains an optional canOperate field; omitting it behaves as false, so older clients keep working unchanged. The control-channel wire vocabulary was already widened to {admin, operator, viewer} by the mymatasan-side change this completes, so no node-side change is required here.
